## Choosing n_bins

Reconstruction error is the mean absolute difference between a value and the value its bin decodes to -- a point mass decodes to itself, any other bin to its midpoint -- as a share of the channel's interquartile range on the training values. `train` is measured on the values the edges were fitted on, `val` on the validation split (2021), which they never saw. `bins` is the number a channel uses: fewer than the candidate only where point masses took exact bins.

| n_bins chosen | 256 |
| why | Reconstruction error falls with every doubling on every channel, on the validation split as on the training values, so the grid has no interior optimum and the finest candidate is chosen. It costs 256 of the bin block's 1,024 fixed identifiers (ADR-0003) and nothing in sequence length, one token per channel per step at any bin count; and it leaves every bin about 13,000 training values or more (3.35 million for pitch and gear oil, 4.5 to 4.7 million for the rest). The tails stay coarse at every candidate. |

## The held-out site against the training range: hill_of_towie

Share of hill_of_towie's values below the lowest training value or above the highest, per calendar year (reported per year, never pooled only: `per_year_sites`). ## Excluded channels
